title: Dombra Five (Домбра бес) - CENTRAL ASIA: DOMBRA FIVE
style:
```
[style: Central Asian Kazakh steppes music, dombra two-string küy, khomus jaw harp drone overtone, doira frame drum, surnay double reed, 5/8 aksak 3+2 limp rhythm, vast steppe landscape, Kazakh spoken verses English chorus, overtone throat singing adjacent, no Western harmony, limp signal metaphor, V4_5ALL]
```
lyrics:
``
[INTRO — dombra solo, küy instrumental style, 3+2 feel]
(Kazakh) Домбыра — dombra / the two-string signal
(Kazakh) Ақсақ — aksak / the limping rhythm

[VERSE 1 — khomus enters bar 2, doira bar 4]
(Kazakh)  Бес — five
(English)  Five beats — the steppe demands
(Kazakh)  Үш пен екі — three and two
(English)  The dombra understands

Aksak means limping — it is not a flaw
The three-then-two is how the steppe was crossed
Every horse that galloped on this land
Moved in five — and never once was lost

(Kazakh)  Даланың жыры — song of the steppe
(English)  Five beats — the signal limps and flies

[PRE-CHORUS — surnay enters]
(Kazakh)  Тыңда — listen
(English)  Three plus two
(Kazakh)  Сез — feel
(English)  The signal's true

[CHORUS — doira full, khomus drone under all]
Dombra five — three and two and move
Aksak rhythm — the steppe's own groove
Khomus buzzes the note between the beats
The signal limps across a thousand sheets

(Kazakh)  Бас сигнал — the main signal
(English)  Five carries it

[VERSE 2 — khomus solo, jaw harp overtone melody 8 bars]
The khomus makes sound from a metal tongue
The mouth is the resonator — the jaw is the room
You cannot separate the instrument from the body
The signal lives inside the player — that is the point

(Kazakh)  Аузы — mouth / resonator
(English)  The signal needs a body to live

[BRIDGE — dombra plays 3 and 2 separately — 3 bars of 3/8, then 2 bars of 2/8, then back to 5/8]
Three alone: even, stable, round
Two alone: clean, clear, decisive
Three plus two: aksak — the limp that covers ground
The steppe is crossed in five

[FINAL CHORUS — full ensemble, surnay piercing above]
Dombra five — three and two and move

[OUTRO — dombra fades to single string pluck, khomus buzzes to silence]
(Kazakh)  Сау бол — be well / goodbye
(English)  The signal crosses the steppe
